decisions.note: Locator 47:110901211 is verified as JP ぜーったい負けられない！. The Vietnamese keeps the emphatic determination and, unlike Chinese 我, does not invent a first-person pronoun absent from the Japanese title.

Locator 47:202072 is verified as JP マイペース. Several Vietnamese treatments are plausible (retain the loan phrase, 'theo nhịp riêng', etc.); defer until the project chooses a consistent policy for katakana English/common-loan skill titles.
Locator 47:100441 is verified as JP いただき☆ストレリチア！. The playful いただき construction and Strelitzia reference are not equivalent to a plain 'I will win'; defer rather than lock the Chinese interpretation.

Locator 47:105201111 is verified as JP まだまだだよ！. This is a conversational Haru Urara title with several natural Vietnamese equivalents; defer for voice-consistent wording rather than using Chinese 我/哦 as fixed evidence.
Locator 47:108402111 is verified as JP アレスの進撃. アレス is the proper name Ares, so the Vietnamese keeps that name instead of generalizing it to Chinese 战神 ('war god').

Locator 47:106103111 is verified as JP 遮るものはない. The Japanese means that nothing obstructs the runner, while Chinese uses a different idiom; several natural Vietnamese titles fit, so defer rather than canonicalize the bridge idiom.
Locator 47:103402111 is verified as JP 扇ノ舞. The noun phrase is unambiguous and 'Vũ điệu quạt' is a compact natural Vietnamese title preserving the fan-dance image.

Locator 47:203002 is verified as JP 手練手管, an idiom about practiced techniques/tactics rather than literal 'wrist/ability'. Multiple Vietnamese idioms are possible; defer instead of following Chinese 手腕 literally.

Locator 47:203431 is verified as JP 才気煥発. The meaning is clear but Vietnamese can naturally choose a formal Hán-Việt or a more idiomatic 'tài năng tỏa sáng' style; defer until that register is reviewed consistently.
Locator 47:203841 is verified as the identical JP idiom 才色兼備. 'Tài sắc vẹn toàn' is the established natural Vietnamese idiom preserving both talent and beauty.

Locator 47:202831 is verified as JP コール&レスポンス ('call and response'). The Chinese localization uses different fan-culture wording; defer until the project chooses whether to retain the English music term or localize it as a Vietnamese hô-đáp expression.
Locator 47:202692 is verified as JP 一番乗り. Depending on title style this can be 'đến đầu tiên', 'đi đầu', or another concise phrase; defer rather than locking the Chinese military-flavored 打头阵.

Locator 47:201601 is verified as JP 地固め, the standard noun for firming/laying a foundation. 'Củng cố nền tảng' is concise, natural Vietnamese and preserves the established gameplay metaphor without over-literal wording.

Locator 47:110602111 is verified as JP お邪魔しま～す♪. This conventional phrase can mean 'xin phép làm phiền/vào nhé' depending on scene and the elongated playful delivery is character-specific; defer for voice-aware treatment.
Locator 47:202522 is verified as JP 型破り. 'Phá cách' is the standard concise Vietnamese expression for breaking conventional forms and fits a compact skill title.
Locator 47:202761 is verified as JP かっとばせ！, a punchy exhortation with sports/baseball-like flavor. Several Vietnamese imperatives are plausible; defer rather than freezing the Chinese wording.

Locator 47:300041 is verified as JP 拡がる恐れ. 恐れ may be read as fear/apprehension/risk depending on title context, so defer until the intended nuance is reviewed instead of treating Chinese 担忧 as authoritative.
